newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Lower on lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Lower on lack of demand.

text.p: Singapore light distillates prices fell on Friday as weak fundamentals take its toll on levels, traders said.
Naphtha levels, weighed down by surplus supplies, weak demand and overnight crude losses shaved off Thursday's gains and settled weaker late Asian trading day.
Traders a poor European market has also dampened sentiment.
The weak fundamentals were evident from the poor awards seen in the Taiwan and Indian tenders.

Taiwan has awarded its tender to buy a second naphtha cargo for August delivery at $195 per tonne. The cargo is for delivery August 15-31. The first cargo for August 1-15 delivery was awarded at $193 per tonne.
The price is lower than its previous tender for a July 20-31 cargo which was awarded at slightly above $215 per tonne.
India has also awarded its tender to sell low aromatic naphtha lifting from Madras July 6-8 at $$21 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.
Its last award for a cargo lifting in June was awarded at $22 per tonne to a South Korean refiner, sources said.
Discussion in the gasoline market was very thin. Spot parcels of 95-octane cargoes were offered at a discount of 40-50 cents fob Singapore but there were not takers.
Talk on Indonesian demand and potential Australian supplies were also absent.
